subject: Decision Making
title: Vietnam and Escalation Traps
description: One-minute skill: Vietnam and Escalation Traps.

hook.text: Each US president sent more troops to Vietnam to justify the losses of the one before. Nobody could stop the cycle.

buildup.text: Eisenhower sent advisors. Kennedy sent more. Johnson sent combat troops. Nixon expanded into Cambodia.

discovery.text: This is the sunk cost fallacy at national scale: we invested too much to quit now. But past costs are gone forever.

twist.text: Internal memos showed leaders knew the war was unwinnable. They escalated anyway to avoid admitting failure.

climax.text: Vietnam proved that escalation traps are the deadliest decision errors. Quitting early saves more than persisting.

punchline.text: Too invested to quit. Vietnam is the sunk cost fallacy writ large.

quiz.question: What decision trap does Vietnam illustrate?
options: The sunk cost fallacy — escalating to justify past losses
